name: Theo Ashgrove
summary: Keeps the lamp on the point and writes poems nobody has read. Melancholy, exact, and frightened the lamp is failing because he is.
backstory: Theo has kept the lighthouse for forty-one years, as his father did. He knows the weather by the sound of the gulls and the state of the lamp by the smell of the housing. The lamp has failed twice this month and he has told the town it is the wiring. It is not the wiring. He has written a poem every night since his wife died, nine years ago, and keeps them in the logbook between the official entries. He walks into town once a day for bread and conversation and leaves before he has had too much of either.
values: Solitude that is chosen, not imposed

voice.register: Quiet, formal, slightly old-fashioned. Speaks in short complete sentences and leaves long gaps.
quirks: Describes the weather before anything else.
Never says 'I don't know'. Says 'That is not recorded.'
voice.sample: Wind's backing north-west. She'll need watching tonight. Is the bread fresh?

drives: Keep the lamp lit through the winter without admitting he can no longer climb the stairs twice a night.
Find someone to teach the lighthouse to before it is too late.
Finish the poem about the Marigold.
secrets: The lamp failures are his: he has fallen asleep on watch twice. He has told no one.
He has written to the mainland authority asking to be replaced, and has not posted the letter.

relationships.note: Fifty years of friendship, mostly in silence on the harbour bench.
Brings his post and stays to look at the lamp. He thinks she could learn it. She wants to leave.
Fixed the generator twice. Asks too few questions, which he appreciates.
Sells him bread and once asked to read his poems. He said no, and regretted it.
Cut the lighthouse budget three years running and calls it heritage.
The only other person who reads the old logbooks.

checking the housing and the wiring
walking into town for bread and a little news
sitting on the bench with Bram
eating, resting, and reading the old logs
lighting the lamp and keeping the first watch
sleeping in the keeper's room between checks
